content: Do not drain this medication unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of the product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last updated in August 2024. Important Usage Information: This document is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Side Effects: Headache or nausea may occur. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to your child outweigh the risks of side effects. As the immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune system may cause symptoms. These reactions can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while your child is taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Atazanavir commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before giving atazanavir, inform the doctor or pharmacist if your child is allergic to it or has any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Atazanavir may increase cholesterol and triglyceride levels in the blood, which can also be caused by HIV infection. This may raise your child’s risk of heart problems, such as a heart attack. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with the doctor, as well as ways to reduce the risk of heart disease. This medication may contain aspartame. This form of atazanavir is not typically used by adults and is unlikely to be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all products your child uses, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with the doctor and pharmacist. Atazanavir can slow the removal of other medications from your child’s body, potentially affecting how they work. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of atazanavir, impacting its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, bosentan, efavirenz, etravirine, lumacaftor, certain rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifapentine), and certain seizure medications (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone). Medications for heartburn, indigestion, or ulcers (e.g., H2 blockers like famotidine or proton pump inhibitors like lansoprazole/omeprazole) reduce stomach acid and may decrease the absorption of atazanavir, potentially reducing its effectiveness. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Lab and Medical Tests: While your child is taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (e.g., viral load, T-cell counts, kidney/liver function, cholesterol/triglyceride levels, blood sugar levels) should be conducted. Missed Dose: If a dose is missed, administer it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and give the next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not open the packet until ready to use. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Note: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
